head: pr17421-r17
report:
I found three defects, all in the Python tool bridge (`src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts`), and I measured each one. I ran out of the 20 minutes before I could probe the other half of the patch: the resume-as-fork claim (`claimResumedSessionOrFork`, `adoptResumedSession`) and the artifact staging code. Nothing below covers those.

## 1. Accept a cell's ended or made-up run id only for `__artifacts_ready__` (P1)

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts:199`, enabled by `:292`

**Mechanism:** `registerPyToolBridge` now also stores every cell's entry in `sessionRegistrations` under the session id alone. When the cell finishes, `unregister()` removes only the `sessionId:runId` key, so that session-level entry stays. The request handler then looks up `registrations.get(registrationKey) ?? sessionRegistrations.get(sessionId)`.

The "Missing run" check at `:195` only stops requests with an empty run. A request that names an ended run, or any invented run, misses the run key, falls back to the newest cell's entry, and runs whatever tool it names. That includes `bash`, `write` and `agent`, using that cell's `ToolSession`, signal and `emitStatus`.

Before this change the fallback was `registrations.get(sessionId)`. Keys are always `${sessionId}:${runId}` (`:282`), so that lookup never matched, and a call from an ended cell got "No active Python tool bridge session". The comment at `:194` says "Everything else still has to say which cell it is", but in practice any run string passes.

The effect: a thread a finished cell left running can now call any tool for as long as the kernel lives. Its effects land in no cell's output, and a cancelled turn does not stop it unless the newest cell's signal was aborted.

**Trigger:** register an entry, call the returned `unregister()`, then POST `{session, run:<old run>, name:"bash", ...}` to `/v1/tool`.

```
$ cd packages/coding-agent && bun test <scratch>/pybridge.test.ts
stale run-1 after unregister -> {"status":200,"body":{"ok":false,"error":"Unknown tool from js runtime: bash"}} toolSession touched: [
  "getToolForEvalBridge", "getToolByName", "getToolForEvalBridge"
]
made-up run -> {"status":200,"body":{"ok":false,"error":"Unknown tool from js runtime: write"}}
```

The probe's `ToolSession` is a stub that has no tools, which is why the call ends in "Unknown tool". What matters is that the request reached tool lookup on the ended cell's session (`getToolForEvalBridge` was called) instead of being refused. With a real session, the tool runs.

**Fix:** use the `sessionRegistrations` fallback only when `runId === ""` and `name === EVAL_ARTIFACTS_READY_BRIDGE_NAME`.

## 2. Stop keeping a cancelled cell's entry as the session's answer for background artifact reads (P2)

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts:292`, with `callSessionToolPromptOnAbort` at `:120`

**Mechanism:** the standing entry is the newest cell's whole entry, including its `abortRequested` and `signal`. If that cell was interrupted or timed out, every later `__artifacts_ready__` call fails at `:120` with "eval cell was interrupted". `prelude._artifact_file` now always goes through the bridge rather than listing the directory, so `read("artifact://N")` from a background thread raises until another cell runs. These are the background readers the patch was written to support, and before this change they could still read by listing the directory locally.

**Trigger:** register an entry with `abortRequested: () => true`, unregister it, then POST `__artifacts_ready__` with `run: ""`.

```
artifacts_ready after cancelled newest cell -> {"status":200,"body":{"ok":false,"error":"bridge call \"__artifacts_ready__\" aborted: eval cell was interrupted"}}
```

## 3. Make the session-entry removal check identity, and release it in per-call mode (P2)

**Files:** `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts:302`; `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/executor.ts:353` and `:434-441`

**Removal is unconditional.** `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession(sessionId)` deletes whatever entry the session id currently maps to. The run-scoped `unregister` guards with `=== entry`; this does not. `shutdownInvalidatedSession` runs it for the old kernel after `replacement.promise` resolves, and the replacement kernel uses the same `sessionId` (`kernel-session-registry.ts:431`). So a cell that already ran on the replacement loses its standing entry, and its background artifact reads fail until the next cell. That this ordering happens in production is an inference. The unconditional delete is measured:

```
$ bun test <scratch>/pybridge2.test.ts
before old-kernel unregister: {"ok":true,"value":"/mnt/nvme/sami/session-tmp/964074-uPVUbCwY/art-cS1KTS/3.bash.log"}
after  old-kernel unregister: {"ok":false,"error":"No active Python tool bridge session: sid-R:"}
```

**Per-call mode never releases entries.** `executePerCall` mints `py-bridge:${randomUUID()}` for each call and shuts the kernel down directly (`executor.ts:441`). `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession` is only called from `shutdownInvalidatedSession`, and grep finds no other call site. Every per-call Python execution therefore leaves a `sessionRegistrations` entry for the life of the process, holding its `ToolSession` and `AbortSignal`. `disposePyToolBridge` (`:307`) clears `registrations` but not `sessionRegistrations` either.

The per-call growth comes from reading the code: `sessionRegistrations` isn't exported, so I couldn't count it. Probe 1 does show that an entry is still reachable after its cell's `unregister()`.

Probes are `pybridge.test.ts` and `pybridge2.test.ts` in the scratch directory, run from `packages/coding-agent`.

**Verdict:** not safe to merge. Finding 1 lets threads from finished Python cells run arbitrary tools.
